H1.note: chain starts at the IL-23 p40 subunit (IL12B); IL12B links to the rest only through a binds (RO:0002436), which does not compose, so the IL12B claim has no route

H2.note: the run's mechanism is loss-of-function (risk alleles weaken the NOD2-LACC1 defense), so each gene's overall effect is protective (neg); no step links NOD2 to the defense process, so the NOD2 claim has no route

H3.note: chain starts at the ligand, so the subject is GPR35; the run's own direction is hedged (expected 'unknown', conflicting mouse knockouts). H3.2 ends at chemotaxis and never reaches the disease, so the claim has no route

findings.detail: H2.1 grounds 'Bacterial muramyl dipeptide' to CHEBI:60539, which is Mo(=O)-bis(molybdopterin guanine dinucleotide), a molybdenum cofactor; muramyl dipeptide is CHEBI:59414, which I used instead.

Chain nodes carry CURIEs of the wrong kind: MDP (a chemical) is tagged 'process' in H2.1; 'GPR35 signaling' is grounded to UniProt:Q9HC97 but tagged 'process' in H3.2; 'Crohn-associated alteration of GPR35 signaling' is grounded to dbSNP:rs3749172 but tagged 'process' in H3.3.
H1 connects IL12B to the chain only through a binds (RO:0002436) edge, which carries no sign and cannot compose, so the IL12B arm has no route to the disease.
H2.1 ends at NOD2 and H2.2 starts at LACC1 feeding a defense process; no step links NOD2 to that process, so NOD2 has no route to Crohn.
H3.2 ends at chemotaxis (a process) but H3.3 starts at the rs3749172 variant; chemotaxis->Crohn is never stated, so GPR35 has no mechanistic route to the disease.

The terminal step (IL-23 signaling process -> Crohn) cites only gene/variant GWAS associations (PMID:17068223, rs11209026, rs6556412); none state a process-level effect with direction, so the step has no valid evidence.

The terminal step (NOD2-LACC1 defense -> Crohn) cites NOD2/LACC1 variant GWAS associations (PMID:11385576, rs2066847, rs3764147) and undirected mouse abnormal-X annotations; none state the defense-process effect.

H3 cites two Gpr35 mouse knockouts with opposite colitis outcomes (MP:0008537 increased vs MP:0008539 decreased susceptibility); after loss-of-function inversion the 'contradicting' one (MP:0008539) agrees with a positive GPR35 effect while the one kept as support (MP:0008537) refutes it, so the two labels are reversed.
H1 is rated 'high' though its IL12B arm has no route and its IL23R terminal step has no valid evidence (only genetic associations at a different node).
H2 is rated 'high' though its NOD2 arm has no route and its LACC1->Crohn terminal step has no valid evidence (only variant associations and undirected mouse phenotypes).

Supporting citations state no chain step: PMID:18587394 and PMID:21102463 (general Crohn GWAS loci, H1), PMID:40089498 and AGR:MGI:2429397:MP:0003009 (LACC1 T-cell variant, Nod2 abnormal cytokine secretion, H2), AGR:MGI:1929509:MP:0013956 (Gpr35 decreased colon length, H3). PMID:27478939 did state a step and was attached to S5.

Several nodes bundle multiple entities under one CURIE: three ligands (KYNA/LPA/5-HIAA) under CHEBI:18344 in H3.1; 'chemotaxis, inflammatory-cell recruitment, and bacterial clearance' under GO:0006935 in H3.2; 'cytokine signaling, autophagy, and bacterial clearance' under GO:0045087 in H2.2/H2.3. Each was expressed as its single grounded term.

The strong human genetics (rs11209026/rs6556412 for IL23R/IL12B; rs2066847/rs3764147 for NOD2/LACC1) is dropped to [] because each chain places its disease link on a downstream process, and the format offers no way to credit a gene- or variant-disease association as support for a process->disease step without a variant->disease step of its own.
